paper.title: Localized exploration in contextual dynamic pricing achieves dimension-free regret

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual dynamic pricing with linear demand model
unmapped: Posted-price dynamic pricing: action is a price in a known interval [l,u]; demand D_t = x_t^T alpha* + p_t (x_t^T beta*) + eps_t, expected revenue p_t * E[D_t] is quadratic in price
Contexts are i.i.d. sub-Gaussian vectors with well-conditioned second-moment matrix (Assumption 1)
Optimal price lies strictly inside [l,u]; intercept and slope x^T alpha*, -x^T beta* in [b1,b2] (Assumption 2)
settings.definition_quote: D_t = x_t^T alpha* + p_t (x_t^T beta*) + eps_t ... eps_t represents random demand shocks, which are assumed to be sub-Gaussian with zero mean and a variance proxy of sigma^2 > 0 ... R(T) = sum_{t=1}^T { r*(x_t) - r_t }

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual linear dynamic pricing, stochastic contexts (lower bound)
unmapped: Posted-price dynamic pricing with linear demand in price and context; parameters in model class M_{b1,b2,rho1,rho2}
settings.definition_quote: For x_t ~ mu satisfying Assumptions 1 and 3, we have inf_pi sup_{theta in M} E[R(T;theta)] >~ sqrt(T).

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual linear dynamic pricing, deterministic contexts (lower bound)
unmapped: Posted-price dynamic pricing with linear demand; contexts x_1..x_T are deterministic (fixed sequence), regret conditioned on x_{1:T}, so the bound holds even for a learner that knows all contexts in advance
settings.definition_quote: For deterministic x_1,...,x_T in X such that ||x_t||_2 <= C_f sqrt(d) ... inf_pi sup_{theta in M} E[ sum_t (r*(x_t;theta) - r(x_t,p_t;theta)) | x_{1:T}] >~ sqrt(T).

symbols.eta: perturbation size of the localized exploration stage

conditions: Assumption 1: i.i.d. sub-Gaussian contexts with well-conditioned second moment
Assumption 2: optimal price inside [l+delta, u-delta]; x^T alpha*, -x^T beta* in [b1,b2]
Assumption 3: anti-concentration of context distribution and non-collinear, non-degenerate alpha*, beta*
tuning: C_0 sqrt((d/sqrt(T)) log T) <= eta <= C_0'

source.label: thm:ub_simple
source.quote: If the planning horizon T is sufficiently large, satisfying T >= C_1 d^4 log^2 T and the hyperparameters are set according to ..., then Algorithm 1 achieves: (a) With probability at least 1 - c T^{-2}, the cumulative regret is bounded by R(T) <= C { sqrt(T) log T + eta^2 T / d }.

results.notes: Probability 1 - cT^{-2}. With eta ~ sqrt((d/sqrt T) log T) the bound becomes C sqrt(T) log T (dimension-free), stated in text after the theorem. Regret is defined via expected revenue r_t.

symbols.eta: perturbation size of the localized exploration stage

tuning: C_0 sqrt((d/sqrt(T)) log T) <= eta <= C_0'

source.label: thm:ub_simple
source.quote: (b) Additionally, the expected cumulative regret satisfies E[R(T)] <= C { sqrt(T) log T + eta^2 T / d }.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected revenue (means), so pseudo-regret. With eta ~ sqrt((d/sqrt T) log T) it gives C sqrt(T) log T.

bound.expression_latex: C \{ \sqrt{\widetilde d T} \log T + \frac{\widetilde d}{2d} \eta^2 T \}

symbols.d_guess: user guess tilde d of the degenerate dimension, with tilde d(eta) <= tilde d <= 2d
symbols.eta: perturbation level solving the critical inequality, eta <= C_0'

tuning: eta <= C_0' solves the critical inequality sqrt(tilde d(eta)/(2d)) >= kappa sqrt(2d/T) log T / eta^2
T_1 = ceil(sqrt(tilde d T) log T)

source.label: thm:ub_main
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. ... If T >= C_1 d log^2 T and the hyperparameters are set according to ..., then (a) With probability at least 1 - c T^{-2}, R(T) <= C { sqrt(tilde d T) log T + (tilde d/(2d)) eta^2 T }.

results.notes: Depends on degenerate dimension defined via eigenvalues of the limiting covariance S*. Text claims refinement to C(sqrt(tilde d)+tilde d/sqrt(tilde d(eta))) sqrt(T) log T for regular solutions and C sqrt(tilde d T) log T if tilde d ~ tilde d(eta). Tuning eta via critical inequality requires spectral information of S*.

bound.expression_latex: \mathbb{E}[R(T)] \le C \{ \sqrt{\widetilde d T} \log T + \frac{\widetilde d}{2d} \eta^2 T \}

symbols.d_guess: user guess tilde d of the degenerate dimension, with tilde d(eta) <= tilde d <= 2d
symbols.eta: perturbation level solving the critical inequality, eta <= C_0'

tuning: eta <= C_0' solves the critical inequality
T_1 = ceil(sqrt(tilde d T) log T)

source.label: thm:ub_main
source.quote: (b) Additionally, the expected cumulative regret satisfies E[R(T)] <= C { sqrt(tilde d T) log T + (tilde d/(2d)) eta^2 T }.

conditions: Gaussian noise N(0, sigma^2) with sigma ~ 1
parameters in model class M_{b1,b2,rho1,rho2} containing an interior point theta-bar in M_{2b1,b2/2,2rho1,rho2-tilde}

source.label: thm:pure-online-lower-bound
source.quote: For deterministic x_1,...,x_T in X such that ||x_t||_2 <= C_f sqrt(d), we have inf_pi sup_{theta in M} E[ sum_t ( r*(x_t;theta) - r(x_t,p_t;theta) ) | x_{1:T} ] >~ sqrt(T).

results.notes: Proved via multivariate van Trees inequality.

conditions: Gaussian noise N(0, sigma^2) with sigma ~ 1
parameters in model class M_{b1,b2,rho1,rho2} containing an interior point theta-bar

source.label: thm:pure-online-lower-bound
source.quote: For x_t ~ mu satisfying Assumptions 1 and 3, we have inf_pi sup_{theta in M} E[R(T;theta)] >~ sqrt(T).

results.notes: Matches the dimension-free upper bound of Theorem 1 up to log T.
